description: A narrative: a bundle WITH prose — the written argument built over a set of member records. Every narrative IS a bundle (it reuses the bundle's member shape: a flat, unordered set of members, each a dual-addressed com.atproto.repo.strongRef pinning an exact content version) and ADDS the argument — either inline `prose` (Markdown, for small narratives) or a `proseBlob` (a Markdown blob, for full papers that exceed the ~150 KiB record limit; exactly one of the two, tooling-enforced) — plus an optional inline `abstract` (a short teaser that rides the firehose), `references` (a map from in-prose citation markers to the records they cite), and optional `figures` (content-addressed image blobs the prose embeds). 'Every narrative is a bundle; not every bundle is a narrative' — the prose is the difference. A paper is a narrative sitting OVER a bundle: its `members` typically holds a SINGLE strongRef to the paper's published tech.scios.rrgi.bundle record (recursive composition), and the prose cites individual nodes inside that bundle via `references`. A narrative may sit over several bundles (members = multiple bundle strongRefs). Citations are content-addressed and rot-proof: the prose carries STABLE keys (never display numbers, never a brittle local ID like 'C-0001'); `references` maps each key to a strongRef plus a cached label; a reading AppView assigns display numbers and renders a reference section at read time, so editing or reordering the prose never breaks a citation (cf. \cite{key}). Each citation is also a live entry point into the graph (resolve the strongRef → expand that node's evidence/support). Figures are NOT discourse nodes: a conceptual diagram is a plain embedded blob; a figure that PRESENTS findings (a data chart) should additionally point, via the figure's optional `subject`, at the evidence node it renders. Evolution is by versioning (a new narrative record + a tech.scios.rrgi.versionOf edge to the prior), so 'living document' and 'frozen citable snapshot' are the same mechanism — every version is an immutable, citable CID. RRGI-authored (no coalition equivalent); intended to be proposed upstream.

name.description: Human-readable title of the narrative (e.g. the paper title).

members.description: The set of member records this narrative is built over (the bundle's shape). Flat and unordered — reading order is carried by `prose`, not this list. For a paper this typically holds a SINGLE strongRef: the paper's published tech.scios.rrgi.bundle record (recursive composition). A narrative may sit over several bundles. Each member is dual-addressed (uri + cid), pinning an exact content version.

items.description: Dual-addressed reference (uri + cid) to one member record — typically the paper's bundle, but may be any record (node, relation, or another bundle).

prose.description: The narrative argument inline, in Markdown — for narratives small enough to fit in the record (an atproto record caps at ~150 KiB; this field caps at 100K chars, the same proven inline bound WhiteWind uses). For full papers use `proseBlob` instead. EXACTLY ONE of `prose`/`proseBlob` must be present (tooling-enforced, since lexicon cannot express oneOf). In-prose citations use stable keys (NOT display numbers, NOT brittle local IDs) in the form [@<key>], where <key> matches a references[].key. Embedded figures use [fig:<key>], where <key> matches a figures[].key. A reading AppView resolves keys, assigns display citation numbers, and renders figures plus a reference section at read time.

proseBlob.description: The full narrative argument as a content-addressed Markdown blob, for narratives too large to inline (an atproto record caps at ~150 KiB, so a full paper's prose does not fit inline alongside its citations and figures; atproto's own guidance is to put large text in a blob). EXACTLY ONE of `prose` (inline) / `proseBlob` (blob) must be present (tooling-enforced). Carries the same [@<key>] / [fig:<key>] markers as `prose`. Like a figure, the bridge fetches and pins this blob on both IPFS nodes — its CID is a native IPFS block CID — so the argument is rot-proof and renderable directly from IPFS, while remaining atproto-native (served by getBlob, federated, and covered by the record's signed proof).

abstract.description: Optional short inline summary/teaser (e.g. the paper's abstract or executive-summary lede). Unlike `proseBlob`, it stays IN the record, so it rides the firehose and powers cards, previews, and search without fetching the prose blob. NOT the full argument.

references.description: The citation manifest: maps each in-prose citation key to the record it cites, with an optional cached label so a reference section can render without resolving every strongRef. The cited records are reachable inside `members` (e.g. by drilling into the bundle); `references` records WHICH of them the prose cites and under WHAT key.

figures.description: Content-addressed image blobs the prose embeds via [fig:<key>] markers. A figure is NOT a discourse node. A conceptual diagram is a plain blob; a figure that presents findings (a data chart) should also set `subject` to the evidence node it renders.

description.description: Optional description of what this narrative IS (metadata about the artifact) — distinct from `prose`, which is the argument itself.

reference.description: One entry in a narrative's citation manifest: a stable key (as it appears in the prose, e.g. [@<key>]) bound to the dual-addressed record it cites. By convention the key is the cited record's rkey (the TID segment of its at-uri) — identity-derived, order-free, and naturally deduped when the same record is cited more than once — but the schema requires only a stable, narrative-unique string; the convention is enforced by tooling, not here.

key.description: The stable citation key used by the prose [@<key>] markers. Unique within this narrative. Never a display number; never a brittle local label (e.g. 'C-0001'). Convention: the cited record's rkey/TID.

subject.description: Dual-addressed reference (uri + cid) to the cited member record (typically a claim or evidence node). CID mandatory, so the citation pins the exact content version and is fetchable from cold storage.

label.description: Optional cached human-readable label (e.g. the cited claim's text) so an AppView can render the reference section without resolving every strongRef. A cache, not the source of truth — the subject's live record is authoritative.

figure.description: One embedded figure: a content-addressed image blob referenced from the prose via a [fig:<key>] marker.

key.description: The stable key used by the prose [fig:<key>] marker. Unique within this narrative.

image.description: The figure image as an ATProto blob (content-addressed; its own CID; dedupes by CID across narratives; archivable). The bridge fetches and pins this blob on both IPFS nodes.

alt.description: Text description of the figure for accessibility and indexing.

caption.description: Optional figure caption rendered beneath the image.

subject.description: Optional dual-addressed reference to the evidence node this figure RENDERS, for a figure that presents findings (a data chart). Conceptual diagrams omit this.
